summary: SDK retry amplification exposes opaque rate-queueing as intermittent streaming latency
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent long-tail streaming responses (~10-30s) and occasional request timeouts while making high-concurrency streaming calls to the Redwood hosted API. Impact: User-facing feature (real-time summaries) degrading intermittently during peak windows; perceived as model slowness/timeouts. Environment: Dedicated account in us-east using SDK v1.3.1 with default retry/backoff settings. Initial hypothesis: model or runtime degradation. Actual root cause (see investigation): server-side windowed rate/soft-429 enforcement combined with aggressive client retries caused request amplification and queueing that manifested as long streaming latencies.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use SDK v1.3.1 default config. 2) Start 40 concurrent streaming requests with small prompt sizes (~50 tokens) at 100 RPS aggregated from a single host. 3) Observe latency distribution: many requests succeed <500ms but a subset shows 10-30s tails or 504s. 4) Repeat under lower concurrency (10 concurrent) and tails disappear. 5) Upgrade to SDK v1.4.2 with adaptive jitter and limiters -> tails disappear.

- 2026-03-10T14:02:03Z request id=rc-01c status=200

Server side traces (sample):

- queue_depth: transient spike to 18 requests
- serving-runtime: token-gen latency per active worker normal (~12ms), but head-of-line wait due to queueing
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-10 customer reported at 14:05; initial triage assumed model regression. Support captured request traces and SDK metrics. Key observations: 1) 429 soft-enforcement was returned during brief bursts (server logs show windowed_count > window_limit). 2) SDK v1.3.1 retries without jitter and with aggressive concurrency produced immediate replays into the same enforcement window. 3) Queue depth on gateway spiked; serving runtime workers were healthy but waiting on queued requests. 4) Reproduced in lab by simulating customer traffic pattern, confirmed that enabling SDK adaptive jitter limiter prevented amplification. 5) Found quota-controller behavior: window resets in ~8s; lack of distributed leaky-bucket smoothing allowed burst bleed-through. Hypothesis validated by: 1) reproducer with SDK v1.3.1 produces long tails and 429s; 2) SDK patch (v1.4.2) with randomized exponential backoff removes tails; 3) short-term server-side mitigation (smoothing window enforcement by adding 250ms random delay on suspected burst origin) reduces queue spikes.

resolution: Root cause: interplay between windowed server-side soft-429 enforcement and aggressive client-side retry/concurrency behavior caused request amplification and head-of-line queueing that presented as long-tail streaming latencies and occasional timeouts. Fixes: 1) Customer guidance: upgrade SDK to v1.4.2 (includes randomized exponential backoff and client-side concurrency limiter) and reduce single-host concurrency for bursty workloads. 2) Server changes: merged quota-controller smoothing (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8321) to add small randomized admission delay to reduce synchronized replays; adjusted window thresholds for dedicated tenants to reduce overshoot. 3) Monitoring: added a dashboard alert for tenant-level queue_depth spikes and 429-rate anomalies and a runbook entry (Confluence link). Workaround applied: temporary smoothing rule in us-east until config rollout completed. Outcome: customer-confirmed stability; issue closed.
postmortem_actions: SDK: ship v1.4.2 and update quickstart examples to recommend concurrency defaults for streaming (max 10 per host)
Platform: quota-controller smoothing merged and rolled to us-east; schedule global rollout
Docs: update troubleshooting guide to surface 429 vs model-slowness patterns and recommended client settings
Monitoring: alert for tenant queue_depth > 10 and 429_rate > 3% sustained for 60s
